canonical_title: Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, 1975-1976
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The Underwood-Miller volume covering 1975-1976, PKD's Fullerton years, when he wrote to scholars and friends explaining the 2-3-74 visions and drafting the theological arguments that grew into the Exegesis.
page_summary:
This volume of the Underwood-Miller Selected Letters gathers Philip K. Dick's correspondence from 1975 and 1976, the years immediately after the 2-3-74 experiences. Living in Fullerton and increasingly consumed by interpreting what had happened to him, PKD used his letters as a laboratory, writing to correspondents such as Claudia Bush, Malcolm Edwards, and others to test formulations of the pink light, Zebra, anamnesis, and the first-century Rome he felt underlay contemporary California.

These are the letters in which the Exegesis effectively goes public in draft. Alongside the metaphysics run the ordinary concerns of a working writer: agents, money, the state of his novels, and the friendships that sustained him.

The volume is a core primary source for the visionary period, showing PKD narrating and re-narrating his experiences in real time to a widening circle of readers.
